modules.module_description:
Catalogue of advanced Python constructs and graph seeding helpers.

This module identifies higher-level language features that the core
inferencer does not immediately convert into type annotations.  It
records occurrences of constructs such as ``TypedDict`` classes,
``NamedTuple`` definitions, magic methods, async functions, ternary
expressions and match/case patterns.  Detected features are added to
an :class:`AdvancedFeatureCatalog`, which is later used by the
annotation phase to insert appropriate type hints or protocol
definitions.

The module defines:

* :class:`AdvancedFeatureKind` - an enumeration of recognised feature
  categories.
* :class:`AdvancedFeatureRecord` - a record describing a single
  occurrence of a feature in the source code (its kind, path, name,
  AST node and optional details).
* :class:`AdvancedFeatureCatalog` - a mutable collection of records
  offering convenience methods to filter by kind or name.
* :class:`AdvancedFeatureAnalysisResult` - a wrapper around a
  catalog returned by the feature seeder.
* :class:`AdvancedFeatureSeeder` - the visitor that walks the AST,
  detects occurrences of advanced features and seeds the contract
  graph accordingly.

The detection logic is currently baked into methods of
``AdvancedFeatureSeeder``.  In future releases, this module may
support a plug-in architecture where external detectors can register
their own feature kinds; see the project report for further
improvement ideas.

modules.module_description:
Agnostic untyped-to-typed conversion pipeline.

The architecture mirrors perfectionist's pipeline: every file gets one
shared :class:`ConversionInput` holding the source text states plus a
parser view (``ast`` tree and token stream) that is built once and
re-derived only after a step actually changes the text — one parse and
one tokenization per text version.  Steps follow perfectionist's
``ToolBase`` contract (``name`` + ``step_count`` + ``process`` with a
keyword-only progress reporter), which maps directly onto the ETA
engine's ``ProcessStep``/substeps model, so every step is visible in
the live progress and the final report.

The default step sequence is Annotate (contract inference and
annotation synthesis), Kwargs (positional-to-keyword call rewriting,
reusing perfectionist's resolver machinery when available), and Format
(the full formatter stage chain).  Every step is parse-gated: output
that fails to parse is discarded in favor of the previous text, so the
pipeline never corrupts a valid file.

modules.module_description:
Shared data models for semantic entities and graph nodes.

This module defines data structures that represent the nodes, edges and
traces used throughout the Semantic Contract Farm. Separating these
definitions into a dedicated module improves cohesion and allows
multiple components (graph construction, advanced feature seeding,
contract negotiation) to depend on a single source of truth.

The key classes exported here are:

* :class:`GraphNodeKind` - an enumeration of the kinds of semantic
  entities represented in the contract graph (modules, classes,
  functions, arguments, variables, attributes, returns, literals,
  containers, calls, conditions, decorators, bases, context managers
  and metaclasses).
* :class:`ContractGraphNode` - a frozen dataclass carrying a
  stable path, node kind, human-readable name and optional AST
  reference. Instances of this class are hashable and can be used as
  dictionary keys.
* :class:`ContractGraphEdge` - a frozen dataclass pairing an
  edge identifier with a type contract. Edges connect two
  ``ContractGraphNode`` instances and describe how evidence flows
  between them.
* :class:`FunctionTrace` and :class:`ClassTrace` - simple containers
  capturing metadata about functions/methods and classes respectively.

top_level_api.name: GraphNodeKind
top_level_api.description:
Kinds of semantic graph nodes.

Each node in the contract graph is annotated with a kind to
describe the semantic entity it represents.  The kinds roughly
correspond to elements of the Python language (modules, classes,
functions) and the positions where type hints may be inferred.

top_level_api.name: ContractGraphNode
top_level_api.description:
One graph node with stable path identity.

Attributes:
    node_id: Unique numeric identifier assigned by the graph.
    path: Qualified path identifying the entity within the module.
    kind: Category of the node (see :class:`GraphNodeKind`).
    name: Human-readable name of the entity (e.g. function or
        variable name).
    ast_node: Optional reference to the originating AST node.

top_level_api.name: ContractGraphEdge
top_level_api.description:
One graph edge backed by a type contract.

Attributes:
    edge_id: Unique numeric identifier for the edge.
    contract: The type contract associated with this edge.  The
        contract describes how type information flows from source to
        target and carries polarity and decay factors.

top_level_api.name: FunctionTrace
top_level_api.description:
Trace metadata for a function or method.

Captures the path to the function, a reference to the AST node,
lists of argument and return paths, and any decorators applied.

top_level_api.name: ClassTrace
top_level_api.description:
Trace metadata for a class.

Captures the path to the class, a reference to the AST node,
information about base classes and decorators, and paths for
``__init__`` and ``__new__`` methods and the metaclass.

program element.  These pieces fall into three broad categories:

  signatures that should override any derived types.

Traceable graph model for type-inference contracts.

This module defines a scope-aware directed graph used by the
Semantic Contract Farm to model relationships between semantic
entities such as modules, classes, functions, arguments,
variables, attributes and return values.  Each node is identified by
a stable qualified path (see :mod:`semantic_contract_farm.paths`),
and edges carry type contracts and evidence with associated
confidence.

The graph is built by the analyzer while walking the AST.  Nodes
represent definitions and usages; edges represent type
constraints (contracts).  Seeds store initial type hints and
confidence scores attached to nodes.  See the README and the
`ContractGraph` class for details on how the graph is used during
propagation and negotiation.

The public API exposes:

* :class:`GraphNodeKind` - an enumeration of node categories.
* :class:`ContractGraphNode` and :class:`ContractGraphEdge` - data
  structures for graph elements.
* :class:`ContractGraph` - container storing nodes, edges, seeds and
  trace metadata.
* Helper classes :class:`FunctionTrace` and :class:`ClassTrace`
  capturing metadata about functions and classes.

modules.module_description:
Import-related data models for semantic code generation.

This module centralises simple data structures used to index and
organise existing imports and classes when generating new code.  The
Semantic Contract Farm analyses the AST of a Python module to
determine what names are already available so that newly generated
type hints, protocols and helper functions can be imported without
colliding with or shadowing existing names.

The key classes provided here are:

* :class:`ExistingImportedName` - records the local name bound by
  an import, along with the originating module, imported name,
  import level and whether the binding comes from an ``import`` or
  ``from … import …`` statement.
* :class:`ExistingModuleImport` - captures a simple ``import module``
  statement, storing the fully qualified module name and the local
  alias used.
* :class:`ExistingNodeContext` - splits a list of existing top-level
  AST nodes into import and class nodes.  It provides a
  ``from_nodes`` class method to build the context from a sequence
  of AST statements.
* :class:`ScriptSymbolIndex` - builds a rich index over existing
  imports and class definitions.  It tracks local class names,
  imported names, module imports, wildcard imports, and provides
  helpers to query whether a simple name is available or whether a
  specific import already exists.

These classes are immutable (where appropriate) and make use of
``@dataclass`` for brevity.  They are designed to be lightweight and
safe to share across analysis passes.

top_level_api.description:
A name already available in the target generation context.

Attributes:
    local_name: The local alias bound by the import statement.
    module: The dotted module path from which the name was imported,
        or ``None`` for relative imports.
    imported_name: The original imported symbol (for ``from`` imports)
        or the module name (for ``import`` statements).
    level: The relative import level (0 for absolute imports).
    is_module_import: Whether the binding comes from a plain
        ``import`` statement instead of ``from``.

top_level_api.description:

A simple container capturing a fully qualified module import and

modules.module_description:
Semantic argument and parameter utilities.

This module defines a small grammar and helper classes for building
function and method signatures in a consistent way.  It exposes
lightweight dataclasses representing different kinds of arguments
(``self``, ``cls``, positional-only, keyword-only, variadic), along
with a normalizer that converts mixed marker/argument sequences into
a uniform list of AST-friendly specs.  By extracting this logic into
its own module the core type-inference engine becomes easier to
understand and extend.  The interfaces here are deliberately
minimalistic: each type holds only the information required to
construct an ``ast.arguments`` node or to compare two signatures.

The main types are:

* :class:`ArgumentSpec` - a single argument with a name, type hint,
  kind and optional default.
* :class:`SelfArgument` and :class:`ClsArgument` - special wrappers
  used to denote the receiver in instance and class methods.
* :class:`SlashMarker` and :class:`StarMarker` - markers for
  positional-only and keyword-only boundaries, matching Python's ``/``
  and bare ``*`` syntax.
* :class:`ParameterState` and :class:`ParameterNormalizer` - mutable
  state and logic used to transform a heterogeneous list of
  :class:`ArgumentItem` objects into a pure tuple of
  :class:`ArgumentSpec` objects respecting positional/keyword rules.

The high-level ``Args`` factory provides convenience constructors for
the various argument kinds.  All of these helpers depend on the
``TypeExpression`` hierarchy for their type hints but avoid importing
concrete classes at module import time to prevent circular imports.
Instead, they perform dynamic imports within methods or default
factories as needed.

Separating argument handling into this module reduces the size of
the core module and clarifies its purpose.  This modular design
aligns with the recommendations in the Google Python Style Guide to
keep functions and modules focused on a single responsibility.

top_level_api.name: ArgumentSpec
top_level_api.description:
Semantic representation of a single function argument.

Each argument has a ``name``, a ``type_hint`` (a type expression
describing the expected value type) and a ``kind`` determining
whether it is positional, keyword or variadic.  A default value
expression may also be provided.  Instances of this class are the
building blocks for constructing ``ast.arguments`` structures.

top_level_api.name: SelfArgument
top_level_api.description:
Special receiver argument representing ``self``.

The default ``type_hint`` is a ``SelfTypeRef`` instance, which
references the class being defined.  To avoid a hard dependency on
the full type expression hierarchy at import time, the factory
function lazily imports and instantiates ``SelfTypeRef`` when
required.  Users can also supply a custom type expression if
desired.

top_level_api.name: ClsArgument
top_level_api.description:
Special receiver argument representing ``cls``.

``ClsArgument`` defaults to ``type[self]``.  It imports
``GenericTypeRef`` and ``SelfTypeRef`` lazily to avoid a direct
dependency on the larger type expression module during import.
A custom ``type_hint`` may be supplied instead.

top_level_api.name: SlashMarker
top_level_api.description: Semantic marker for Python's ``/`` positional-only indicator.

top_level_api.name: StarMarker
top_level_api.description: Semantic marker for Python's bare ``*`` keyword-only indicator.

top_level_api.name: Args
top_level_api.description:
Factory namespace for common argument constructors.

This class contains only ``@staticmethod`` methods so it does not
maintain any state.  It exists purely to group together
convenience functions for creating different kinds of arguments.

top_level_api.name: ParameterState
top_level_api.description:
Mutable state used while normalizing argument sequences.

As the normalizer processes a mixed list of arguments and markers,
this state object keeps track of whether the slash or star markers
have been seen, and whether variadic positional or keyword
arguments have been encountered.  Violations of Python's signature
syntax (e.g., two slashes or ``**kwargs`` appearing twice) are
signalled by raising a :class:`SemanticCodegenError` via the
``fail`` function imported at runtime from
:mod:`semantic_contract_farm.exceptions`.

top_level_api.name: ParameterNormalizer
top_level_api.description:
Normalize mixed argument and marker sequences.

The normalizer takes a tuple of :class:`ArgumentItem` objects and
produces a tuple of :class:`ArgumentSpec` objects that conform to
Python's signature rules.  Positional-only arguments and slash
markers are converted to positional-only specs, bare stars and
subsequent arguments become keyword-only specs, and variadic
arguments are handled accordingly.  Any misuse of markers (e.g.,
two slashes or a bare star after ``*args``) will raise a
``SemanticCodegenError``.

top_level_api.name: ProtocolGrammar
top_level_api.description:
Infer protocol names and docstrings from method signatures and names.

When the inference pipeline synthesises a protocol to represent
structural typing requirements, it often lacks a meaningful class
name and documentation.  The grammar analyses the names and
signatures of the protocol methods to derive semantic *capabilities*.
Dunder methods map to well-known behaviours such as ``__iter__`` →
``Iteration`` and ``__call__`` → ``Call``.  Verb-prefixed methods
like ``read_*`` or ``write_*`` translate to capabilities like
``Reading`` or ``Writing``.  Composite capabilities combine
complementary operations (e.g. ``__iter__`` and ``__next__`` →
``Iterator``).

The derived capabilities inform both the generated class name
(prefixed with ``Supports``) and the docstring, which lists the
human-readable names of the required behaviours and method set.
Individual method docstrings are generated when absent, using the
capability to describe the expected behaviour succinctly.  See
:meth:`infer` for the main entry point.

modules.module_description:
Protocol specification and indexing utilities.

This module collects the dataclasses and helpers related to protocol
generation and reuse.  In the Semantic Contract Farm a "protocol" is
a structural interface defined by a set of method signatures.  These
classes describe protocol methods (:class:`MethodSpec`), entire
protocols (:class:`ProtocolSpec`) and registration results
(:class:`ProtocolRegistration`).  The :class:`ProtocolShape` and
``ExistingProtocolIndex`` classes provide a way to compare existing
classes in the source code to potential protocol specifications so
that already-defined protocols can be reused instead of generated
anew.

top_level_api.name: MethodSpec
top_level_api.description:
Semantic protocol method specification.

Each method has a ``name``, a tuple of argument items (see
:class:`~semantic_contract_farm.parameters.ArgumentItem`), a
return type expression and optional docstring and decorators.
The ``body`` may hold a tuple of statements if an implementation
stub is required; otherwise it can be ``None`` to indicate that
the protocol only declares the signature.

top_level_api.name: ProtocolSpec
top_level_api.description:
Semantic protocol specification.

A protocol consists of a tuple of method specifications.  Optional
metadata includes the protocol name, a docstring, base classes
expressed as type expressions and decorators applied to the class.
A missing name or docstring indicates that they should be inferred
automatically based on method semantics.

top_level_api.name: ProtocolRegistration
top_level_api.description:
Result of registering or reusing a protocol class.

When the code generator registers a protocol, it either finds an
existing class matching the requested shape and returns it
(``is_existing`` set to ``True``) or constructs a new class
definition and returns it.  The ``match_reason`` indicates whether
the match occurred by name, by structural shape or whether a new
protocol was generated.

top_level_api.name: ProtocolShape
top_level_api.description:
Comparable structural shape of a protocol class.

A ``ProtocolShape`` is a sorted tuple of method names paired with
their argument names (including markers for varargs).  Two
protocols with the same shape are considered equivalent for reuse
purposes.

top_level_api.name: ExistingProtocolIndex
top_level_api.description:
Index existing protocol classes by name and method shape.

This helper scans a collection of ``ClassDef`` nodes and records
those that derive from ``Protocol`` (either directly or via a
``typing.Protocol`` alias).  It can then be queried either by
protocol name or by method shape to determine whether a matching
protocol already exists in the source file.

top_level_api.name: MethodSemanticProfile
top_level_api.description:
Semantic summary of one protocol method.

A ``MethodSemanticProfile`` captures a method's name, the inferred
capability (a human-readable verb describing its semantic action),
the number of required arguments and whether the method is a
dunder (special) method.  These profiles are used by the
``ProtocolGrammar`` to infer protocol names and docstrings.

modules.module_description:
Typeshed stub integration for the contract graph.

This module defines helper classes to incorporate return-type information
from Python stub files (typeshed) into the contract graph used by the
Semantic Contract Farm.  When analysing untyped code, the contract
graph builder seeds a few literal and builtin conversions but knows
nothing about the return types of imported functions or methods on
standard library classes.  As a result, many call expressions default
to ``object``.  By consulting the typeshed stubs for the modules
imported in a file, we can add high-confidence type candidates for
those calls and attribute accesses before the negotiation step.  This
improves the precision of the inferred types without relying on ad hoc
heuristics.

The main components provided here are:

* :class:`StubSignatureLoader` - parses one or more stub files and
  records the return type of every top-level function and class method
  encountered.  It uses the existing ``TypeshedStubParser`` from
  :mod:`semantic_contract_farm.typeshed_inference` and stores results in
  dictionaries keyed by module name, function name, class name and
  method name.

* :class:`ContractGraphStubSeeder` - given a contract graph, a
  loaded stub catalog and a symbol index describing the imports in
  the source module, this seeder walks the graph and adds ``TypeSeed``
  evidence for call and attribute nodes based on stub return types.
  For example, if ``Path`` was imported from ``pathlib`` and the code
  accesses ``p.name``, this seeder will look up ``Path.name`` in
  ``pathlib/__init__.pyi`` and seed a ``str`` type at the attribute
  path with a high confidence.  Similarly, calls to imported
  functions like ``math.sqrt`` will receive a stub-derived return
  type.

The seeder does not attempt to perform call-site type-parameter
inference; it simply uses the annotation provided by the stub.  It is
expected that subsequent propagation and negotiation phases will
refine generic types further.

This integration is optional; the caller must construct a
``StubSignatureLoader`` with a path to a typeshed tree and pass it
along with a ``ScriptSymbolIndex`` to the seeder.  If a stub file is
missing or a signature cannot be found, the seeder gracefully skips
that node.

top_level_api.name: StubSignatureLoader
top_level_api.description:
Load and cache return-type signatures from typeshed stub files.

Given the root of a typeshed tree, this loader provides on-demand
parsing of ``.pyi`` files for a given module.  It stores two
dictionaries:

* ``_function_returns`` mapping ``(module, function)`` to a
  :class:`~semantic_contract_farm.type_expressions.TypeExpression` giving
  the function's return type.
* ``_method_returns`` mapping ``(module, class, method)`` to a
  :class:`~semantic_contract_farm.type_expressions.TypeExpression` for
  the method's return type.

The loader uses :class:`TypeshedStubParser` from
:mod:`semantic_contract_farm.typeshed_inference` to parse stub files.  If
a stub file is missing or cannot be parsed, no entries are
created.  Lookups on unloaded modules trigger a parse of the
corresponding stub file.  The typeshed tree is expected to
contain a ``stdlib`` directory mirroring the standard library
package structure (as in the official typeshed repository).

top_level_api.name: ContractGraphStubSeeder
top_level_api.description:
Add typeshed-derived type seeds to a contract graph.

This seeder iterates over every node in the contract graph and
inserts additional ``TypeSeed`` evidence derived from typeshed
signatures.  It uses the loader to obtain return types for
functions and methods imported in the analysed module.  The
provided ``ScriptSymbolIndex`` is used to map local names back to
their originating modules.  A small amount of logic reconciles
attribute accesses with method signatures: if a variable has been
classified as an instance of a particular class, the stub for that
class is consulted for the attribute name.

top_level_api.name: ContractNegotiator
top_level_api.description:
Negotiate type beliefs across the contract graph until stability.

The negotiator implements the "ant-farm" propagation algorithm
described in the project report: candidate type hints (ants)
traverse contracts (paths) in the graph, combining and narrowing
beliefs at each node.  Propagation continues until the total
information entropy of all beliefs stabilises or a configured
iteration/event limit is reached.  The current implementation
includes several micro-optimisations:

* Cached configuration attributes are stored in local variables to
  avoid repeated attribute lookups inside hot loops.
* Early exit is performed when no beliefs change and the message
  queue is empty, skipping an unnecessary entropy calculation.
* Event counts prevent runaway propagation when the graph is
  extremely connected.

These enhancements improve performance on large stress fixtures
without altering the semantics of the negotiation.

modules.module_description:
Utilities for Python 3.13 type aliases.

This module defines a collection of dataclasses and helpers to support
the synthesis of parameterised type aliases under PEP 695.  The
definitions here are imported by the core semantic engine but live in
their own module to improve modularity.  To avoid circular import
problems, any references back into the type expression modules are
performed lazily inside method bodies rather than at import time.

top_level_api.name: TypeAliasParameterKind
top_level_api.description: Kinds of Python 3.13 type-alias type parameters.

top_level_api.name: TypeAliasTypeParameterSpec
top_level_api.description:
Semantic description of a type parameter for a PEP 695 type alias.

Python 3.13 introduces parameterised ``type`` aliases which can bind
``TypeVar``, ``ParamSpec`` or ``TypeVarTuple`` parameters.  This
dataclass captures the name of the parameter, its kind
(type variable, parameter specification or type-variable tuple) and
optional bound and default.  The helper constructors
:meth:`typevar`, :meth:`paramspec` and :meth:`typevartuple` make it
easy to instantiate the appropriate kind.  Use :meth:`to_ast` to
convert the specification into the corresponding ``ast.type_param``
node when emitting an ``ast.TypeAlias``.

top_level_api.name: TypeAliasSpec
top_level_api.description:
Semantic specification for a ``type`` alias in Python 3.13.

A ``type`` alias associates a new alias name with a target
type expression, optionally parameterised over one or more type
parameters.  This dataclass bundles the alias name, the
canonicalised value to alias and any type parameters (see
:class:`TypeAliasTypeParameterSpec`).  A semantic key computed by
:meth:`key` combines the alias value and parameter kinds, allowing
reuse detection across distinct alias names.

top_level_api.name: TypeAliasRegistration
top_level_api.description:
Result of registering a semantic type alias with the manager.

When adding a type alias, the manager either reuses an existing
``ast.TypeAlias`` node (matched by name or value) or builds a new
node.  This dataclass records the associated specification, the
alias node itself, whether it already existed in the parsed module,
and the reason for the match (``"name"``, ``"value"`` or ``"new"``).

top_level_api.name: TypeAliasNameInferer
top_level_api.description:
Infer sensible PascalCase names for generated type aliases.

When no explicit alias name is provided, the manager derives one
from the aliased type expression.  Names are formed by extracting
a canonical word from the underlying expression (for example
``List[int]`` yields ``ListAlias``) and converting it to
PascalCase.  All inferred names are suffixed with ``Alias`` to
indicate their purpose.  The validator ensures that the result is a
valid Python identifier.

top_level_api.name: ExistingTypeAliasIndex
top_level_api.description: Index existing Python 3.13 type aliases by name and value text.

top_level_api.name: TypeAliasNodeBuilder
top_level_api.description:
Construct ``ast.TypeAlias`` nodes from semantic specifications.

This helper validates alias names, converts type parameters to their
corresponding ``ast.type_param`` nodes using a
:class:`TypeExpressionResolver`, and renders the alias value into
an ``ast.expr`` suitable for runtime evaluation.  The resulting
``AstTypeAlias`` can be inserted into a module body.  See
:class:`TypeAliasSpec` for the semantic input.

top_level_api.name: TypeAliasManager
top_level_api.description:
Manage semantic type aliases with reuse and automatic name inference.

The manager keeps track of existing type aliases in a module and
synthesises new ones on demand.  When adding an alias, it first
consults the existing alias index to detect matches by name or by
alias value, returning a :class:`TypeAliasRegistration` that
indicates whether an existing alias was reused.  If no match is
found, the manager uses the :class:`TypeAliasNameInferer` to
generate a fresh PascalCase name (unless an explicit name was
provided) and builds a new ``ast.TypeAlias`` node via the
:class:`TypeAliasNodeBuilder`.  Registrations are recorded so that
:attr:`nodes` returns only the newly created alias nodes for
insertion into the code.  Duplicate value alias requests share the
same name, ensuring a single canonical alias per distinct type
expression.

top_level_api.name: TypeUnionSimplifier
top_level_api.description:
Normalize, sort, deduplicate and generalize union members.

Union types (PEP 604) can quickly become unwieldy when many
observations are merged.  This simplifier performs a number of
normalisation steps on a set of candidate type expressions:

* **Flattening** nested unions into a single options list.
* **Deduplication** of semantically identical types (preserving the
  first occurrence).
* **Literal collapsing**: when all literal values of a given primitive
  type (e.g., ``Literal[1, 2]`` and ``Literal[3]``) are covered by
  an existing builtin like ``int``, the literal options are removed.
* **Numeric collapsing**: ``bool | int | float`` is simplified to
  ``float`` (the widest numeric type) while preserving non-numeric
  options.
* **Generic generalisation**: unions of container types with the same
  semantic family (e.g., ``list[str] | tuple[str]``) are collapsed
  to the appropriate ``collections.abc`` ABC such as
  ``MutableSequence[str]`` or ``Sequence[str]``.  Similarly, mapping
  unions are collapsed to ``Mapping`` or ``MutableMapping``.
* **Sorting**: the resulting options are sorted deterministically
  according to builtin precedence and their semantic keys, so that
  equal unions compare equal and rendering order is stable.

If a collapse limit is provided and the number of simplified options
exceeds the limit, the simplifier returns ``object`` to avoid
enormous unions.  See :meth:`simplify` for the entry point.

Specifications and registries for type parameters.

This module encapsulates the machinery for synthesizing ``TypeVar`` and
``ParamSpec`` declarations.  It defines simple dataclasses to record
the semantic signatures of type parameters (constraints, bounds and
variance) and the selected identifier name.  A registry class is
provided to allocate stable short names for parameters based on their
semantic identity, avoiding clashes and making generation deterministic.

top_level_api.name: TypeVarSignature
top_level_api.description:
Semantic identity of a generated ``TypeVar``.

The signature records the upper bound (if any), a tuple of
constraint types, and variance flags.  Two type variables are
considered identical if their signatures match.

top_level_api.name: ParamSpecSignature
top_level_api.description:
Semantic identity of a generated ``ParamSpec``.

Parameter specifications may have an optional bound and variance flags.

top_level_api.name: TypeVarSpec
top_level_api.description:
Complete specification for a generated ``TypeVar``.

A type variable specification consists of a chosen identifier name
and its associated :class:`TypeVarSignature`.  Instances of this
class are typically produced by a :class:`TypeParameterNameRegistry`.

top_level_api.name: ParamSpecSpec
top_level_api.description:
Complete specification for a generated ``ParamSpec``.

The ``name`` holds the chosen identifier, and the ``signature``
captures any bound and variance information.  Convenience methods
are provided to obtain references to the full parameter, its
``args`` and its ``kwargs`` components.

top_level_api.name: TypeParameterNameRegistry
top_level_api.description:
Allocate stable names for ``TypeVar`` and ``ParamSpec`` specs.

When the type inference engine needs to introduce new type
parameters, it queries this registry with a semantic key (derived
from the parameter's signature) and an optional requested name.
The registry ensures that each unique signature is assigned a
deterministic short name (e.g., ``T``, ``U``, ``P``) and that no
two distinct signatures share a name.  Explicitly requested names
are honoured unless they would clash with a previously used name.

modules.module_description:
Local type inference: per-scope variable typing + expression typing.

Shared by autotype (RHS → annotation) and autokwargs (receiver typing
so positional → keyword rewrites can resolve stdlib methods). Together
with :data:`~perfectionist._resolution.stdlib_registry.STDLIB_REGISTRY`
this implements *receiver chain inference* — propagating types along
expressions like ``Path(p).read_text().splitlines()``.

All CST traversal is registered through autoast's
:class:`~perfectionist.autoast.LibCstVisitor`; nothing here subclasses a
libcst visitor. :class:`InferenceCallbacks` maintains a
:class:`TypeEnvironment` as the walk enters/leaves function scopes and
binds assignment targets to inferred types; :class:`ExpressionTyper`
answers "what type is this expression?" by recursing through the same
environment and the shared :class:`CallResolver`.

modules.module_description:
Call resolver: maps a libcst ``Call`` node to a :class:`ResolvedCall`.

Resolution priority:

1. Local in-file functions and classes (definition collector).
2. Imports (``import x`` / ``from x import y``) routed through the
   shared :class:`ProjectIndex`.
3. Class methods on locally-resolvable receivers (constructor-typed
   variables, classmethod/staticmethod calls on indexed classes).
4. Stdlib fallback via the typeshed-lite :data:`STDLIB_REGISTRY`
   (constructors like ``Path(...)``, module functions like
   ``json.loads(...)``, and receiver-typed methods like
   ``Path.read_text`` when the caller supplies ``receiver_type``).

Anything outside that — astroid, full typeshed — is deferred. A failed
resolution returns ``None`` and the consumer (the tool) decides what to
do.

modules.module_description:
Typeshed-lite stdlib return-type registry.

Covers the stdlib surface that ``demo.py`` exercises so the
:class:`~perfectionist._resolution.resolver.CallResolver` can answer
return-type queries for stdlib calls without astroid or typeshed.

Entries are keyed two ways:

* ``functions[(module, name)]`` — top-level callable
  (``json.loads`` → ``object``, ``re.compile`` → ``Pattern[str]``).
* ``methods[(receiver_type, method)]`` — bound method on a known type
  (``("Path", "read_text")`` → ``str``).

Receiver types are the *names* the registry produces (``Path``,
``Counter``, ``Pattern[str]``, ``Match[str]``, …); the chain-inference
pass propagates them as it walks RHS expressions.

top_level_api.name: StdlibEntry
top_level_api.description:
One registered callable: return type + (optional) receiver type.

``element_from_arg`` opts a container constructor into *element-type
inference*: when set, the ``[object]`` placeholder in ``return_type``
is refined from the element type of the positional argument at that
index — so ``Counter(text.split())`` (arg 0 typed ``list[str]``)
yields ``Counter[str]`` rather than the bare ``Counter[object]``.

``positional_only_count`` marks the first *n* ``parameter_names`` as
positional-only (the ``/`` marker): C builtins like ``len(obj, /)``
reject keyword calls, so autokwargs must never promote them even
though their return type is still useful for inference.

top_level_api.description: Read-only registry of stdlib return types + receiver-method types.

top_level_api.description:

``Counter[str].most_common`` carries ``list[tuple[{element}, int]]``;
the receiver's ``str`` argument is substituted to yield
``list[tuple[str, int]]``. A receiver with no type argument (or an
entry without the placeholder) is returned unchanged.

modules.module_description:
Picklable type database mined from typeshed stubs.

This module defines the *data contracts* and *query surface* for a
build-time-extracted database of builtin and stdlib type signatures. The
companion :mod:`perfectionist._resolution.typeshed_extract` script parses
typeshed ``.pyi`` stubs and pickles a :class:`TypeDatabase`; tools then
unpickle it and consult it during inference.

Design goals:

* **Render-ready** — every annotation is stored as exact source text
  (``list[int | dict[str, int | str]]``) so a tool can drop it straight
  into a type hint, *plus* a structured :class:`TypeExpr` tree for
  programmatic queries.
* **Import-aware** — every non-builtin symbol referenced by an
  annotation carries its import provenance (``Iterable`` →
  ``collections.abc``), so a tool knows exactly what to add to the
  import block.
* **Operator-aware** — the marquee query, :meth:`TypeDatabase.binary_op`,
  answers ``left <op> right`` (``str * int -> str``, ``int / int ->
  float``, ``Path / "x" -> Path``) by resolving the relevant ``__dunder__``
  / reflected ``__rdunder__`` overloads.
* **Callable-aware** — module-level builtins (``len``, ``open``,
  ``sorted``) are captured alongside class methods, so a tool can resolve
  a free-function call's return type and keyword names, and consult any
  call name uniformly via :meth:`TypeDatabase.lookup`.
* **Picklable** — only module-level frozen dataclasses, tuples, frozensets,
  strings, and a :class:`~enum.StrEnum`; no closures or local types.

top_level_api.name: SymbolImport
top_level_api.description:
Import provenance for one non-builtin symbol in an annotation.

``public`` is ``False`` for typeshed-internal sources
(``_typeshed``, ``_collections_abc``) that cannot be imported at
runtime: a consumer should widen such a type (e.g. to ``object``)
rather than emit an unusable import.

top_level_api.name: TypeExpr
top_level_api.description:
A structured, render-ready type annotation.

* ``text`` — exact source (``dict[str, int | str]``), drop-in ready.
* ``head`` — outermost constructor/base name (``dict``); ``""`` for a
  union or a bare special form.
* ``args`` — generic arguments or union members as child
  :class:`TypeExpr` nodes.
* ``is_union`` — ``True`` when ``args`` are union members (``A | B``).
* ``imports`` — every non-builtin symbol used *anywhere* in the tree,
  with import provenance.

modules.module_description:
libcst-driven autorestore.

Replaces the line-fingerprint pipeline with a structural one:

1. Both the *original* and the *transformed* source are parsed via
   :class:`~perfectionist.autoast.AutoAst.parse_libcst_module`.
2. The original module is walked once through autoast's
   :class:`~perfectionist.autoast.LibCstVisitor` and every comment that
   matches a known lint-suppression directive is harvested together
   with the structural key of the statement that carries it.
3. The transformed module is walked the same way; whenever a
   transformed statement's key matches one harvested from the original,
   the comment is re-attached (trailing inline or leading line) via
   ``node.with_changes(...)``.
4. The patched tree is rendered back via
   :class:`~perfectionist.autoast.AutoAst.render_libcst_module`, so the
   parsed CST stays the source of truth and is automatically refreshed
   after restoration — no string surgery, no tokenize bookkeeping.

The structural key is the libcst code of the statement *with all
comments stripped*. Keys are hashed and used both for exact matching
and (when not found) for a difflib similarity fallback.

modules.module_description:
RAM-disk / tempdir workspace utility used by the pipeline.

``AutoStorage`` provides an isolated workspace under one of these backends
(highest priority first):

- **Linux tmpfs** — a private directory under ``/dev/shm`` when that
  filesystem is mounted (true RAM-backed).
- **macOS ram disk** — when ``hdiutil`` and ``diskutil`` are on PATH and
  ``allow_native_ramdisk=True`` (off by default — creating a ram volume
  prompts for permissions / takes seconds, so we'd rather use tmpfs).
- **Tempdir fallback** — ``tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`` on every other
  platform or when ``kind="temp"`` is requested explicitly.

The pipeline uses this for two purposes:

1. **Source-text staging** — when the user passes raw Python source as
   a positional argument, autostorage writes it under the workspace so
   the rest of the pipeline can treat it as a regular file path.
2. **Pre-write staging** — every transformed file is materialized
   inside the workspace first and then atomically copied to the
   final destination. This keeps partial writes off the user's tree
   on Ctrl-C and gives the diff renderer a stable file to read.

modules.module_description:
libcst-based variable annotation injector with chain inference.

Walks every :class:`Assign` and adds an :class:`AnnAssign` annotation
when the right-hand side's type can be resolved. Resolution flows
through the shared :class:`~perfectionist._resolution.ExpressionTyper`,
so constructor calls, literals, stdlib calls, and *chained* receiver
expressions (``Path(p).read_text().splitlines()``) are all handled.

Scope is tracked through :class:`~perfectionist._resolution.TypeEnvironment`:
function parameters with annotations are seeded on entry, and each
resolvable assignment binds its target so later statements in the same
scope can chain off it. Re-assignments are bound (to keep inference
current) but never re-annotated.

top_level_api.name: _ParamEvidence
top_level_api.description:
Per-function evidence for typing an otherwise-bare parameter.

Each map is keyed by parameter name. ``comparison`` records the
literal type a name is tested against (``mode == "x"`` → ``str``);
``methods`` accumulates the method names invoked on a name
(``value.upper()`` → ``{"upper"}``), later resolved to the unique
owning type through the stdlib registry's structural index;
``passed_to`` accumulates ``(callable, position)`` slots a name is
handed to (``Path(p)`` → ``{("Path", 0)}``), resolved to the type the
callable imposes on that slot; ``operator`` records a type an operator
imposes on a name (``"ab" * n`` → ``n: int`` by sequence repetition);
``narrowed`` records a function-wide ``assert isinstance(name, T)``
guarantee (``assert isinstance(x, (int, float))`` → ``x: float``);
``arithmetic`` collects names used as operands of numeric arithmetic
(``a + b`` / ``total * scale``), which default to ``float`` when no
stronger signal applies; ``nullable`` collects names tested against
``None`` (``value is None``), which widen their otherwise concrete
type to ``T | None``.

top_level_api.name: _AssignTrace
top_level_api.description:
Per-name local-variable assignment history for union/retry typing.

``types`` is the distinct RHS types seen across every assignment to
one name, in first-appearance order; ``annassign`` is the first
emitted :class:`AnnAssign` for that name, the node whose annotation is
upgraded to a union when a later assignment introduced a new type
(``probe = 0`` then ``probe = "x"`` → ``probe: int | str``).
``value`` and ``walk_type`` capture the first emitted assignment's RHS
node and the type resolved for it during the walk, so a name assigned
exactly once (``count == 1``) can be re-typed at signature time once
inferred parameter types are seeded (``c = Counter(text.split())`` →
``Counter[str]`` after ``text: str`` is known).

that includes any non-numeric name is returned unchanged.

modules.module_description:
Detect code-like regions inside docstring text so they survive reflow.

Three kinds of regions are recognized:

- **Doctest blocks** — lines starting with ``>>>`` and their ``...``
  continuations plus the immediately following output lines.
- **Fenced code blocks** — text between triple-backtick or triple-tilde
  fences (Markdown / reST style).
- **Indented code blocks** — paragraphs whose every line is indented
  by at least four spaces *and* parse as Python source.

Regions are returned as ``(start, end)`` line index spans (half-open).
Callers reflow only the lines outside these spans.

modules.module_description:
Extract numeric magic values (in comparisons) into named constants.

Supports four scopes:

- ``module``    — hoist to top-level ``NAME: int|float = value`` definitions
- ``function``  — emit ``name: int|float = value`` at the top of the enclosing
  function body; lookups stay bare names
- ``class``     — emit ``NAME: ClassVar[int|float] = value`` at the top of the
  enclosing class body; lookups become ``self.NAME`` / ``cls.NAME`` /
  ``ClassName.NAME`` depending on the surrounding method's nature
- ``off``       — disable extraction

Only literals that appear inside a ``Comparison`` are extracted.

The visit/leave plumbing lives entirely in
:mod:`~perfectionist.autoast`. This module exposes a plain Python
class that registers callbacks against a
:class:`~perfectionist.autoast.LibCstVisitor`.
